mainTopic: Cooking for animals and גויים on יום טוב, inviting a גוי, and the משניות on fire, insulating food and רבן גמליאל's stringencies
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא about the word לכם in the פסוק that allows cooking on יום טוב. רבי יוסי הגלילי says it excludes animals. רבי עקיבא says it excludes גויים, because you must feed your animals but not גויים. אביי then asks how date pits may be thrown to animals according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, and רב יוסף explains that they are fit for fuel on יום טוב and can be carried on bread on שבת. Next the גמרא brings רבי יהושע בן לוי: you may invite a גוי on שבת but not on יום טוב, in case you cook extra for him. רב אחא בר יעקב forbids it even on שבת because of the גוי's forbidden leftover wine, and the הלכה is publicly taught like רבי יהושע בן לוי. A new משנה follows about heating water and making a fire on יום טוב, and a ברייתא shows that only בית הלל allow the fire. A third משנה lists three cases where רבן גמליאל was strict like בית שמאי. The גמרא begins explaining the case of keeping hot food warm without an עירובי תבשילין, and רב הונא's ruling continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוסי הגלילי: "for you" and not for dogs
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי הגלילי learns from the word לכם that cooking on יום טוב is allowed only for people, not for dogs.
steps.simpleTranslation: "For you" means not for dogs. This is the view of רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יוסי הגלילי's reading of the word לכם in the פסוק about יום טוב cooking. Food preparation is permitted for people only, not for animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק permits food preparation on יום טוב, but it adds the word לכם, "for you." רבי יוסי הגלילי reads that word as a limit: the permission covers only humans, so dogs and other animals are left out.

keyTerms.meaning: "For you": the word in the פסוק that limits the permission
Dogs, standing for animals in general
Festival day, when food preparation is allowed

phrases.english: "For you" — and not for dogs,
these are the words of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא on the פסוק of יום טוב cooking, which the גמרא began citing just before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food may be prepared on יום טוב only for people, not for animals.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: animals are included, gentiles are excluded
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא says "every soul" includes animals, and the word לכם instead comes to exclude גויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: even an animal's soul is included. If so, why does the פסוק say "for you"? For you, and not for גויים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with רבי יוסי הגלילי. He includes animals and uses לכם to leave out גויים instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא focuses on the words כל נפש, "every soul," which sound wide enough to include animals. Since animals are included, the word לכם must exclude someone else, and he says it excludes גויים.

keyTerms.meaning: Included in the meaning of the words
"What does the פסוק come to teach?": asks why a word is needed

steps.confusionAlert: Both תנאים use the same word לכם to exclude something. They only argue about WHAT it excludes: dogs (רבי יוסי הגלילי) or גויים (רבי עקיבא).

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says:
even the soul of an animal is included in the meaning.
phrases.notes: He is reading the words "every soul" (כל נפש) in the same פסוק.

phrases.english: If so, what does the verse teach by saying "for you"?
For you, and not for gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an opposing reading of the same פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Food may be prepared for animals on יום טוב, but not for גויים.

steps.title: Why include dogs but exclude gentiles?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks רבי עקיבא's side why animals go in and גויים go out, and not the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: What did you see that made you include dogs and exclude גויים?
steps.whatsHappening: A question is raised about רבי עקיבא's choice. This sets up the reason given in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words כל נפש could include both animals and גויים, and לכם could exclude either one. The question asks what logic decides which group is included and which is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: "What did you see?": asks for the reason behind a choice

phrases.english: And what did you see to include the dogs
and to exclude the gentiles?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the logic of רבי עקיבא's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for including animals and excluding גויים, rather than the reverse.

steps.title: You must feed your animals, but not gentiles
steps.stepSummary: Animals are included because their owner is responsible for feeding them. גויים are excluded because you have no such duty to feed them.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include dogs because feeding them is your responsibility. I exclude גויים because feeding them is not your responsibility.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer gives the reason: responsibility for feeding decides who counts as "for you."
steps.deeperAnalysis: Your own animals depend on you for food, so cooking for them is like cooking for your own household. A גוי is not someone you are obligated to feed, so cooking for him falls outside the permission of לכם.

keyTerms.meaning: "Their food is on you": you are responsible to feed them

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי עקיבא, the test is responsibility to feed. Your animals depend on you, so they are included. גויים do not, so they are excluded.

phrases.english: I include the dogs
because their food is upon you,
phrases.notes: Meaning, you are responsible for feeding your own animals.

phrases.english: and I exclude the gentiles
because their food is not upon you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The deciding factor is the duty to feed: animals depend on you, גויים do not.

steps.title: אביי: how can we throw date pits to animals?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב יוסף: according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, who excludes animals, how may we throw date pits to animals on יום טוב?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, who says "for you and not for dogs," how do we throw these date pits to animals on יום טוב?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges a common practice based on רבי יוסי הגלילי's view. Date pits are not human food, so why are we allowed to handle them on יום טוב?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If animals' needs do not count on יום טוב, then something that is only animal food has no permitted use. It should be מוקצה and forbidden to move. Yet people throw date pits to animals on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Items set aside and forbidden to handle on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Yosef:
And according to Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, who said
"for you" and not for dogs,
these date pits, to the animals
how do we throw them on a Festival?
phrases.notes: People don't eat date pits, so the worry is that they should be מוקצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבי יוסי הגלילי's view from step 1 and tests it against common practice.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי הגלילי's view that animals' needs do not count on יום טוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If animal food has no permitted use on יום טוב, date pits should be מוקצה, yet we throw them to animals.

steps.title: רב יוסף: the pits are fit for fuel
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that date pits are not מוקצה because they can be burned as fuel, which is a permitted human use.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: since they are fit for burning.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains that date pits have a human use, as fuel. So they are not מוקצה and may be handled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pits don't need to be human food to escape מוקצה. A person can use them to feed a fire for cooking. Since they may be handled for that reason, they may also be thrown to animals.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Since they are fit for fuel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Finds a different permitted use that removes מוקצה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Date pits are only animal food, so they would be מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They have a human use as fuel, so they may be handled.

steps.title: What about wet date pits?
steps.stepSummary: The answer works for dry pits, but wet pits don't burn, so why may they be handled?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for dry ones. For wet ones, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רב יוסף's answer. Wet pits are not good fuel, so the fuel answer seems not to apply to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's answer depends on the pits being burnable. Moist pits don't burn well, so they seem to have no human use and should still be מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: "It works out": the answer fits one case but not another

phrases.english: This works out well with dry ones;
with moist ones, what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 6 using the case of wet pits.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wet pits are not usable fuel, so the answer does not cover them.

steps.title: Wet pits are fit for a big fire
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that even wet pits can be burned in a large fire, so they also have a human use.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: they are fit for a big fire.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף defends his answer. A large fire can burn even wet pits, so they are fuel too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wet pits won't burn in a small fire, but a big fire dries them out and burns them. So wet pits also have a human use, are not מוקצה, and may be given to animals even according to רבי יוסי הגלילי.
steps.whatToRemember: Even according to רבי יוסי הגלילי, date pits may be given to animals on יום טוב. This is not because animal needs count. It is because the pits, dry or wet, are fit for fuel and so are not מוקצה.

phrases.english: He said to him:
They are fit for a large fire.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's follow-up challenge about wet pits.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extends the original answer to cover the hard case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wet pits cannot be fuel, so they should be מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A large fire burns even wet pits, so they too are fit for fuel and not מוקצה.

steps.title: Fuel works on יום טוב, but what about שבת?
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף again. Burning pits for fuel only helps on יום טוב, so how may date pits be handled on שבת?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works on יום טוב. But on שבת, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי accepts the 'fuel' answer for יום טוב. He points out that it cannot work for שבת, when lighting a fire is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף's whole answer depended on the pits being usable as fuel. On שבת you may not burn anything, so the pits have no permitted human use that day. That should make them מוקצה again.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It works out fine' — granting one case before challenging another
'What is there to say?' — the case is still unexplained
An item set aside from use, which may not be moved on שבת or יום טוב

phrases.english: This works out well on a Festival,
phrases.notes: He means the answer that the pits can be burned, since lighting a fire for cooking is allowed on יום טוב.

phrases.english: on Shabbat, what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: תִּינַח בְּיוֹם טוֹב, בְּשַׁבָּת מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the fuel answer from Steps 6 and 8, then shows that it cannot work for שבת.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's 'fuel' explanation for why date pits are not מוקצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fuel use only exists where burning is allowed. On שבת burning is forbidden, so the pits should be מוקצה.

steps.title: On שבת the pits are carried on bread
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף answers that on שבת the pits are moved together with bread, following שמואל's rule that a person may use bread for all his needs.
steps.simpleTranslation: We move them together with bread. This follows שמואל, who said: a person may do all his needs with bread.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives a new way to move the pits on שבת. You place them on a piece of bread and carry the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pits are not moved directly. They come along on the bread, which may be moved. שמואל's rule shows that using bread as a tray like this is not disrespectful to the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: A person may use bread for all his needs

phrases.english: We move them along with bread.
phrases.notes: He means you put the pits on a piece of bread and carry the bread.

phrases.english: Like Shmuel, for Shmuel said:
A person may do all his needs with bread.

steps.whatToRemember: On יום טוב the pits may be handled because they can be burned. On שבת they are carried on bread, following שמואל's rule.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שבת challenge from Step 9.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New method of handling: moving the pits by means of a permitted item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without fuel use, the pits cannot be moved at all on שבת.
steps.terutzMaskana: The pits may be moved on שבת by carrying them on bread, which שמואל allows.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי forbids inviting a גוי on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the lenient ruling about cooking when גויים are present argues with רבי יהושע בן לוי. He allows inviting a גוי on שבת but not on יום טוב, in case the host cooks more for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רבי יהושע בן לוי, who said: you may invite a גוי on שבת, but you may not invite a גוי on יום טוב. This is a rabbinic safeguard, in case you cook more for his sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of cooking for גויים. It brings רבי יהושע בן לוי, who disagrees with the earlier lenient view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת there is no cooking at all, so a גוי guest causes no problem. On יום טוב cooking is allowed for Jews, so the host might add extra food for the גוי. That would be forbidden, since you may not cook for a גוי on יום טוב.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it argues with' — the גמרא points out a disagreement
We invite (as a guest for a meal)
In case he cooks more for his sake

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהושע בן לוי is not saying a גוי is forbidden to eat Jewish food. He fears only that the host will cook extra on יום טוב for the גוי.

phrases.english: And it disagrees with Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi,
phrases.notes: 'It' is the more lenient ruling on the previous amud, which allowed cooking when גויים are also eating.

phrases.english: for Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
We may invite a gentile on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְזַמְּנִין אֶת הַגּוֹי בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: but we may not invite a gentile on a Festival,
a safeguard decree, lest he add more for his sake.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the date-pit discussion. It returns to the lenient ruling from the previous amud about cooking when גויים also eat, and notes that רבי יהושע בן לוי disagrees with it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rest of the section. The next view, רב אחא בר יעקב's, makes this ruling even stricter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: You may invite a גוי on שבת but not on יום טוב, in case you cook extra for him.

steps.title: רב אחא בר יעקב forbids it even on שבת, because of leftover wine
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב says that even on שבת you may not invite a גוי, because of the wine left over in his cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: Even on שבת, no, because of the leftover wine in the cups.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives a stricter view. He forbids inviting a גוי even on שבת, for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is no longer extra cooking. Once a גוי drinks from a cup, the wine left in it becomes forbidden. The host might then come to move that forbidden leftover wine on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Even on שבת it is also not allowed
Leftover wine remaining in the cups

phrases.english: Rav Aḥa bar Ya'akov said:
Even on Shabbat as well, no,
because of the leftovers in the cups.
phrases.notes: He means the wine a גוי leaves in his cup. That wine becomes forbidden, so it may not be moved.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ בְּשַׁבָּת נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes further than רבי יהושע בן לוי in Step 11 and forbids the invitation on שבת too.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not invite a גוי even on שבת, because his leftover wine is forbidden and would be מוקצה.

steps.title: Then our own cup leftovers should be a problem too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if leftover wine is a problem, the leftovers in Jewish cups should be forbidden to move as well.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, ours too!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב. Every meal leaves wine in the cups, including the cups Jews drink from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack assumes the problem is that leftover drink is useless junk. If that were the reason, it would apply equally to Jewish cups. Yet nobody forbids moving those.

phrases.english: If so, ours too!
phrases.notes: He means the wine left in the cups Jews drink from.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אחא בר יעקב's reason from Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's claim that cup leftovers are a problem
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If leftovers are useless and so מוקצה, Jewish cup leftovers would also be מוקצה.

steps.title: Our leftovers can be given to chickens
steps.stepSummary: The answer: leftovers in Jewish cups have a use, since they can be given to chickens.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ours are fit for chickens.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that Jewish leftovers are still useful. That keeps them from being מוקצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An item that has a permitted use is not מוקצה. Leftover wine can be poured out for chickens, so it has a use.

phrases.english: Ours are fit for chickens.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction: one item has a permitted use, the other is assumed to have none
steps.terutzHavaAmina: All cup leftovers are useless and so מוקצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Jewish leftovers can feed chickens, so they are not מוקצה.

steps.title: The גוי's leftovers can also feed chickens
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: the גוי's leftovers could also be given to chickens.
steps.simpleTranslation: Theirs are also fit for chickens!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the chicken answer. If chickens can drink our leftovers, they can drink the גוי's leftovers too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The chicken answer seems to work for every cup. If so, it does not explain why the גוי's cup should be any different.

phrases.english: Theirs too are fit for chickens!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer from Step 14 back against רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.kashyaTarget: The chicken answer as a way to tell Jewish leftovers apart from the גוי's
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Chickens could drink the גוי's leftovers too, so those should not be מוקצה either.

steps.title: The גוי's leftover wine is forbidden for any benefit
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the גוי's leftover wine is אסור בהנאה. You may not even feed it to chickens, so it has no use at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: Theirs are forbidden for any benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the real difference. Wine a גוי drank from may not be used for any benefit, even feeding animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Feeding chickens counts as getting benefit. Since the גוי's leftovers are אסור בהנאה, that use is forbidden too. So they have no permitted use and are מוקצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Items forbidden for any benefit at all

phrases.english: Theirs are items forbidden for benefit.

steps.whatToRemember: Jewish cup leftovers may be moved because they can feed chickens. A גוי's leftover wine is אסור בהנאה, so it has no use and is מוקצה.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 15 and backs up רב אחא בר יעקב.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Clarifies the halachic status of the item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גוי's leftovers can feed chickens just like ours.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גוי's leftovers are אסור בהנאה, so even feeding chickens is forbidden.

steps.title: Why not move the leftover wine along with the cup?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the forbidden leftovers cannot be moved along with the cup. רבא allows moving a coal pan for its ashes even though useless wood chips are on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let him move them along with the cup! Didn't רבא say: you may move a coal pan for the sake of its ashes, even though there are broken pieces of wood on it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב אחא בר יעקב's reason. It quotes רבא's ruling, which allows moving something forbidden together with something permitted. The answer comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cup itself may be moved. רבא's case shows that a forbidden item resting on a permitted item can be carried along with it. If so, the leftover wine should be no reason to forbid inviting a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Didn't [so-and-so] say?' — brings a source to challenge

phrases.english: Then let him move them along with the cup?
Didn't Rava say:
We may move a coal pan for the sake of its ashes,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִיכָּא עֲלֵיהּ שִׁבְרֵי עֵצִים!
phrases.english: even though there are broken pieces of wood on it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְטַלְטְלִינְהוּ אַגַּב כָּסָא? מִי לָא אָמַר רָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts from Step 16 that the leftovers are forbidden. Asks why they still cannot be moved together with the cup.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אחא בר יעקב's ruling that leftover wine is a reason not to invite a גוי on שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבא allows moving a permitted item together with something forbidden on it. So the cup could be moved with the forbidden wine inside.

steps.title: Wood chips are only מוקצה, but the wine is forbidden for any benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the comparison to רבא's coal pan. The wood chips there are not אסור בהנאה, but the גוי's wine is.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, the wood chips are not forbidden for benefit. Here, the wine is forbidden for benefit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 17. רבא's coal pan case does not apply here, because the two cases involve different kinds of איסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wood chips on the coal pan are only מוקצה. They may not be moved on their own, but they are not forbidden in any deeper way. The גוי's leftover wine is אסור בהנאה, which is a much stronger איסור, so you cannot carry it along with the cup the way the chips are carried with the ashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Things you may not benefit from at all

phrases.english: There, they are not things forbidden for benefit,
phrases.notes: "There" means רבא's coal pan with the useless wood chips, from step 17.

phrases.english: here, they are things forbidden for benefit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the step 17 challenge by showing that רבא's case is different.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Forbidden leftovers could be carried along with a useful cup, just like the wood chips are carried with the ashes.
steps.terutzMaskana: That leniency only works for things that are just מוקצה. It does not work for things that are אסור בהנאה.

steps.title: Treat the cups like a chamber pot
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא מדפתי suggests the cups should be removable the way a disgusting chamber pot may be removed on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא from דפתי said to רבינא: Let it be like a chamber pot of waste!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא מדפתי offers another reason the cups should be allowed to be moved. A chamber pot may be taken away on שבת because it is disgusting, so these cups should be no different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known leniency for גרף של רעי: even though it is מוקצה, you may remove it because it is repulsive to leave it there. Cups with forbidden wine left on the table are also unpleasant, so the same leniency should apply.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַחָא מִדִּפְתִּי לְרָבִינָא:
phrases.english: Rav Aḥa from Difti said to Ravina:
But let it be like a chamber pot of waste!
phrases.notes: A chamber pot may be taken out on שבת because it is disgusting to leave it around.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the coal pan comparison fails, a new comparison is offered.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that the cups with forbidden wine may not be moved
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Disgusting מוקצה items like a chamber pot may be removed, so the cups should be removable for the same reason.

steps.title: You may not create a chamber pot situation on purpose
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that the chamber pot leniency is only for a situation that already exists. You should not set one up deliberately.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Does one make a chamber pot of waste from the start?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא agrees that a chamber pot may be removed. But he says no one should create such a mess on purpose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leniency for גרף של רעי applies only after the situation has already happened. It is not permission to bring about a disgusting מוקצה situation לכתחילה. Bringing the גוי to the table and leaving forbidden wine in the cups would be creating that problem on purpose.
steps.confusionAlert: רבינא does not say a chamber pot may not be removed. He says you should not put yourself into that situation to begin with.

phrases.english: He said to him:

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי עוֹשִׂין גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי לְכַתְּחִלָּה?
phrases.english: And does one make a chamber pot of waste from the start?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי עוֹשִׂין גְּרָף שֶׁל רְעִי לְכַתְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אחא's comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the leniency (after the fact versus from the start)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The chamber pot leniency would allow removing the cups.
steps.terutzMaskana: That leniency only applies after the fact. You may not set up such a situation לכתחילה.

steps.title: מר שמואל's public ruling on inviting a גוי
steps.stepSummary: מר שמואל, speaking with רבא's approval, teaches that you may invite a גוי on שבת but not on יום טוב, in case you cook extra for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא appointed מר שמואל to speak, and he taught: One may invite a גוי on שבת, but one may not invite a גוי on יום טוב. This is a גזירה, in case he cooks more for the גוי's sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the practical bottom line for this topic. Inviting a גוי is fine on שבת but not on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On שבת no cooking is allowed at all, so having a guest cannot lead to cooking. On יום טוב you may cook food for Jews, so a host might cook extra for the גוי, which is not allowed. The חכמים made a גזירה against inviting him to prevent this.

keyTerms.meaning: He appointed him (to give a public lecture)
A protective decree of the חכמים
In case he cooks more for him

steps.whatToRemember: Inviting a גוי: permitted on שבת, forbidden on יום טוב, because on יום טוב you might cook extra for him.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה. The ruling follows רבי יהושע בן לוי, so a גוי may be invited on שבת, despite רב אחא בר יעקב's worry about leftover wine.

phrases.english: Rava appointed Mar Shmuel to speak,
and he taught publicly:
One may invite a gentile on Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין מְזַמְּנִין אֶת הַגּוֹי בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: but one may not invite a gentile on a Festival,
a decree, in case he cooks more for his sake.
phrases.notes: Cooking on יום טוב is only allowed for Jews, so cooking extra for the גוי would be forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final practical ruling. It follows רבי יהושע בן לוי (step 11) and permits inviting a גוי on שבת, against רב אחא בר יעקב's stricter view (step 12).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Inviting a גוי is permitted on שבת and forbidden on יום טוב, because of a גזירה that the host might cook extra for him.

steps.title: How מרימר and מר זוטרא handled a visiting גוי on יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: When a גוי happened to visit on יום טוב, these אמוראים told him he was welcome to what they had, but they would not cook anything extra for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: מרימר and מר זוטרא, when a גוי happened to visit them on יום טוב, would tell him: If you are happy with what we prepared for ourselves, good. If not, we will not go to extra trouble for your sake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells how two אמוראים acted when a גוי showed up on his own on יום טוב. They kept to the rule by making clear that nothing extra would be cooked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מר שמואל's גזירה is against inviting a גוי. Here the גוי came by himself, so they did not send him away. They protected against the real concern, cooking extra for him, by telling him so openly.

keyTerms.meaning: It is acceptable to you, you are satisfied

phrases.english: Mareimar and Mar Zutra,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הֲוָה מִקְּלַע לְהוּ גּוֹי בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: when a gentile happened to come to them on a Festival,
they would say to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִי נִיחָא לָךְ בְּמַאי דִּטְרִיחָא לַן מוּטָב,
phrases.english: If you are satisfied with what we troubled to make for ourselves, good;
and if not, extra trouble
for your sake we will not take.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָרִימָר וּמַר זוּטְרָא כִּי הֲוָה מִקְּלַע לְהוּ גּוֹי בְּיוֹם טוֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the יום טוב concern was handled in practice when a גוי was not invited but came anyway.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A גוי who comes on his own on יום טוב may eat what is already prepared, but nothing extra may be cooked for him.

steps.title: New משנה: heating water on יום טוב for washing feet, and warming oneself by a fire
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי allow heating water on יום טוב only if it is fit for drinking. בית הלל permit it even for washing feet. A person may also make a fire to warm himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: בית שמאי say: A person may not heat water for his feet unless it is fit for drinking. בית הלל permit it. A person may make a fire and warm himself by it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It brings a מחלוקת about heating water on יום טוב for washing, then states that making a fire to warm oneself is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי allow fire on יום טוב only for food and drink, so the water must at least be drinkable. בית הלל permit heating water even just for washing feet. The final line permits making a fire for warmth, which also is not food preparation.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (start of a new משנה)
A bonfire, a fire for warmth

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a new topic: whether you may use fire on יום טוב for bodily needs beyond food, like washing and warming up.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Beit Shammai say:
A person may not heat water for his feet
unless it is fit for drinking.
And Beit Hillel permit it.
A person may make a fire
and warm himself in front of it.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים לֹא יָחֵם אָדָם חַמִּין לְרַגְלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the previous discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי allow heating water on יום טוב only if it is drinkable. בית הלל permit it even for washing feet. Making a fire to warm oneself is permitted.

steps.title: Who taught the rule about making a fire?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the lenient rule that one may make a fire to warm himself is everyone's opinion, or only בית הלל's.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages asked: this rule about a fire, who taught it? Is it everyone's view, and בית שמאי make a difference between warming the whole body and warming just one limb? Or did only בית הלל teach it, and בית שמאי make no such difference?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks who taught the last line of the משנה, the one that allows making a fire to warm yourself on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי forbid heating water just to wash your feet. The question is whether they might still allow a fire that warms your whole body, because that benefit is bigger, like the benefit of food. If so, the fire line is everyone's view; if not, it belongs only to בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open question the Sages could not settle right away)

phrases.english: GEMARA: A question was raised before them:
This fire, who taught it?
phrases.notes: This is the last line of the משנה from step 23: a person may make a fire to warm himself.

phrases.english: Is it everyone's opinion,
and בית שמאי make a difference

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין הֲנָאַת כׇּל גּוּפוֹ לַהֲנָאַת אֵבֶר אֶחָד,
phrases.english: between benefit to the whole body and benefit to one limb,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא בֵּית הִלֵּל קָתָנֵי לַהּ,
phrases.english: or perhaps בית הלל taught it,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל בֵּית שַׁמַּאי לָא שָׁנֵי לְהוּ?
phrases.english: but בית שמאי do not make that difference?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who stands behind the final clause of the משנה quoted in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether בית שמאי agree that making a fire to warm the whole body is allowed, or whether only בית הלל allow it.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows only בית הלל allow it
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says openly that בית שמאי forbid making a fire to warm oneself and בית הלל allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: בית שמאי say a person may not make a fire and warm himself by it, and בית הלל allow it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא. בית שמאי clearly forbid making a fire for warmth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because בית שמאי forbid even the whole-body warming, they do not make a difference between whole body and one limb. So the line in the משנה allowing a fire was taught only by בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Come and hear (the גמרא brings a source to answer)

steps.whatToRemember: The fire-for-warmth leniency belongs to בית הלל alone. בית שמאי forbid it, just like heating water to wash feet.

phrases.english: Come and hear: בית שמאי say:
A person may not make a fire
and warm himself in front of it.
And בית הלל allow it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the question of step 24 with an explicit ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Only בית הלל taught the fire leniency. בית שמאי forbid it and make no whole-body versus one-limb difference.

steps.title: Three cases where רבן גמליאל was strict like בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה lists three things where רבן גמליאל followed the strict view of בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: In three things רבן גמליאל was strict like בית שמאי: you may not put away hot food to keep it warm on יום טוב from the start; you may not set up a lamp on יום טוב; and you may not bake thick loaves, only thin ones.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists three יום טוב cases where רבן גמליאל ruled strictly, following בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the הלכה follows בית הלל, so it stands out that רבן גמליאל was strict here. Thick loaves take more work than thin ones, which is why the strict view limits them.

keyTerms.meaning: Head of the Sages, from the family of הלל
Wrapping up hot food to keep it warm

phrases.english: MISHNA: Three things

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַחְמִיר כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי:
phrases.english: רבן גמליאל is strict like the words of בית שמאי:
We do not wrap up hot food to keep it warm
phrases.notes: This is about a יום טוב on Friday, when you want the food to stay warm for שבת.

phrases.english: from the start on יום טוב,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין זוֹקְפִין אֶת הַמְּנוֹרָה בְּיוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: and we do not set up the lamp on יום טוב,
and we do not bake thick loaves
but only thin ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מַחְמִיר כְּדִבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, still about where בית שמאי and בית הלל differ on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל, following בית שמאי, forbids insulating hot food on יום טוב from the start, setting up a lamp on יום טוב, and baking thick loaves.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל points to his father's house
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל supports his strict view: in his father's house they never baked thick loaves on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said: in my father's house they never baked thick loaves, only thin ones.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל brings proof for the third case from how his own family acted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses his family's practice as a source for the law. He treats what was done in his father's house as showing what the הלכה is. The next step shows why the חכמים reject this proof.

phrases.english: רבן גמליאל said:
In all the days of my father's house
they did not bake thick loaves
but only thin ones.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל מִימֵיהֶן שֶׁל בֵּית אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the third case of the משנה (thick loaves).
steps.raayaObject: That thick loaves may not be baked on יום טוב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The practice of רבן גמליאל's father's household.

steps.title: The חכמים: your family was strict only for themselves
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that his father's house was strict on themselves but allowed all of ישראל to bake thick loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: what can we do about your father's house? They were strict for themselves, but lenient for all of ישראל, allowing them to bake thick loaves and coal-baked cakes.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back on רבן גמליאל's proof. His family's custom was a personal strictness, not a ruling for everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Watching what someone does for himself does not prove the law, because he may be extra careful. His family's actual ruling for the public was lenient, so the proof actually backs the lenient side.
steps.whatToRemember: A great person's private strictness is not proof of the law. What he rules for everyone else is what counts.

phrases.english: They said to him:
What shall we do about your father's house,
who were strict on themselves
and lenient for all of ישראל
to bake thick loaves and coal-baked cakes.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ מָה נַעֲשֶׂה לְבֵית אָבִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof רבן גמליאל brought in step 27.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from his father's household.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The family's practice was a personal stringency. Their public ruling was lenient.

steps.title: What case is insulating hot food about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the case has an עירובי תבשילין or not, and shows that either way one side is hard to explain.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he set up an עירובי תבשילין, why do בית שמאי forbid it? And if he did not, why do בית הלל allow it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the first case of the משנה, insulating hot food on יום טוב for שבת. It asks what exact situation the משנה means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עירובי תבשילין allows preparing on יום טוב for שבת. With one, בית שמאי's ban makes no sense; without one, בית הלל's permission makes no sense. So both readings seem to have a problem.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What situation are we talking about?
Food set aside before יום טוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת

steps.confusionAlert: This is not about cooking on יום טוב for יום טוב itself. It is about a יום טוב on Friday, when you prepare for שבת, which normally needs an עירובי תבשילין.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the case?
If he set up an עירובי תבשילין,
what is the reason of בית שמאי?
And if he did not set up an עירובי תבשילין,
what is the reason of בית הלל?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the first case of the משנה in step 26 to define its circumstances.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the משנה is talking about a case with or without an עירובי תבשילין, since each choice makes one side hard to explain.
steps.kashyaTarget: Both possible readings of the dispute about insulating hot food.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With an עירוב, בית שמאי's ban is hard to explain; without one, בית הלל's leniency is hard to explain.

steps.title: רב הונא: no עירוב, but basic needs were allowed
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says the case is without an עירובי תבשילין, and the חכמים still allowed what a person needs to live.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: really, the case is where he did not set up an עירובי תבשילין, and the חכמים allowed him what he needs for his basic living.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question by choosing the case with no עירובי תבשילין. He explains why בית הלל still allow it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even without an עירוב, the חכמים did not leave a person with nothing for שבת. They allowed him enough for his basic needs, and to בית הלל that includes wrapping up hot food. בית שמאי do not give this allowance, so they forbid it.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually (I stick with this option)

steps.whatToRemember: Without an עירובי תבשילין, בית הלל still allow a person to prepare his basic needs for שבת, like keeping his hot food warm.

phrases.english: רב הונא said:
Really, I will tell you
that he did not set up an עירובי תבשילין,
and the Sages allowed him enough for his basic living.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא לְעוֹלָם אֵימָא לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided question of step 29 by choosing the second option.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the question and explains the hard part with a special allowance.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without an עירובי תבשילין, nothing at all may be prepared for שבת, so בית הלל's leniency seems unexplained.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even without an עירוב, the חכמים allowed basic needs, and בית הלל count insulating hot food as one of them.

steps.title: רב הונא is consistent with his own ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רב הונא's answer matches his known ruling: someone without an עירובי תבשילין still gets one loaf baked and one pot cooked for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא follows his own reasoning, because רב הונא said: someone who did not set aside an עירובי תבשילין may have one loaf of bread baked for him and one pot of food cooked for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רב הונא's answer by quoting another ruling of his that says the same idea. The quote continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 30, רב הונא said that even without an עירובי תבשילין, the חכמים allow what a person needs to live. Here the גמרא shows this is his steady view. Even when someone forgot the עירוב, he still gets the basic minimum: one loaf and one pot.

keyTerms.meaning: Following his own reasoning; consistent with his other rulings
Food set aside before יום טוב that allows cooking on יום טוב for שבת

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think one loaf and one pot means full permission to cook. It is only the bare minimum a person needs. Full cooking still needs an עירובי תבשילין.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that forgetting the עירוב does not leave a person without food for שבת. The minimum he needs is still allowed.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna follows his own reasoning,
as Rav Huna said:
One who did not set aside an eruv tavshilin —
they bake for him one loaf of bread,
and they cook for him one pot of food,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב הוּנָא לְטַעְמֵיהּ, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 30 by showing רב הונא holds the same view elsewhere.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's claim that even without an עירובי תבשילין, the minimum a person needs is permitted
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב הונא's own separate ruling: one loaf and one pot may be prepared for someone who did not make an עירובי תבשילין
